records.title: Ferroportin deficiency drives olaparib resistance in ovarian cancer via the cGAS-STING-STAT3 survival axis.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains the most lethal gynaecological malignancy, and acquired resistance to PARP inhibitors such as olaparib represents a major clinical challenge. Although dysregulation of iron metabolism has been implicated in tumorigenesis, the specific role of the iron exporter SLC40A1 (ferroportin, FPN) in mediating olaparib resistance remains poorly understood. The study aimed to elucidate the clinical significance of FPN deficiency and to explore therapeutic strategies for reversing olaparib resistance. FPN expression was evaluated in OC samples from a clinical cohort of 19 patients, stratified by olaparib responsiveness, to determine its prognostic value. Functional mechanisms were investigated using multiple OC cell lines, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and mouse xenograft models. We integrated analyses of iron homeostasis, ROS dynamics, DNA repair capacity, and innate immune signaling, with a focus on the cGAS-STING-STAT3 signaling cascade. The therapeutic potential of combining olaparib with the ferroptosis inducer erastin or the STING inhibitor C-176 was assessed as a strategy to overcome FPN deficiency-driven resistance. Clinically, FPN expression was significantly downregulated in olaparib-resistant tissues compared with sensitive controls (p < 0.05), and low FPN levels were strongly associated with poor therapeutic outcomes. Mechanistically, FPN deficiency promoted intracellular iron accumulation and ROS generation, which led to increased ferroptosis vulnerability, impaired homologous recombination repair (HRR) and concomitant activation of the cGAS-STING-STAT3 inflammatory axis, thereby driving olaparib resistance. Notably, in vivo studies demonstrated that combining olaparib with either erastin or C-176 significantly suppressed tumour growth and restored drug sensitivity compared with monotherapy (p < 0.01), supporting the translational potential of targeting this axis. Our study establishes a clinically relevant mechanistic connection between ferroportin deficiency and cGAS-STING-STAT3-mediated olaparib resistance in OC. We identify the FPN-ROS-cGAS-STING-STAT3 axis as an actionable vulnerability in resistant OC, indicating that this pathway is a promising therapeutic target to overcome olaparib resistance. FPN loss drives olaparib resistance and predicts poor outcomes in ovarian cancer. FPN loss causes iron and ROS accumulation, impairing HRR and activating the cGAS-STING-STAT3 axis. The cGAS-STING-STAT3 pro-survival program drives olaparib resistance. STING inhibition restores olaparib sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer.

records.title: Macrophage Polarization in Sarcoidosis: Implications for Granuloma Formation, Fibrosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
records.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disease with a complex and incompletely understood immunopathogenesis. Macrophages and T lymphocytes play pivotal roles in granuloma formation and disease progression through dynamic interactions involving cytokine signaling and immune regulation. Recent evidence suggests that macrophage polarization, particularly the balance between classically activated M1 macrophages and alternatively activated M2 macrophages, plays a critical role in inflammatory granuloma formation and fibrotic progression in pulmonary sarcoidosis. TH1-related cytokines, including interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), promote proinflammatory M1 polarization, whereas TH2-related cytokines, such as interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13, drive M2 polarization, tissue remodeling, and fibrosis. Emerging transcriptional, single-cell spatial transcriptomic, and 3D organoid studies further demonstrate the remarkable heterogeneity of macrophages in sarcoid granulomas. Current and emerging therapeutic approaches, including corticosteroids, methotrexate, anti-TNF agents, leflunomide, Janus kinase inhibitors, and novel macrophage-targeted strategies (such as efzofitimod), may exert their effects, in part, by modulating these distinct macrophage activation pathways. This review summarizes the available evidence on macrophage polarization in sarcoidosis and provides an immunology-informed clinical framework for disease endotyping, biomarker-guided monitoring, and targeted therapeutic strategies to prevent fibrotic progression.

records.title: Generation of a senescent synovial organoid model using rat synovial fibroblasts treated with oxidative stress.
records.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common age-related joint disease characterized by cartilage loss and synovitis. Cellular senescence contributes to chronic inflammation through senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs). Recent evidence indicates that senescent synovial fibroblasts (SFs) contribute to OA pathogenesis. However, the in vitro modeling of the microenvironment formed by senescent SFs via SASPs remains limited. Here, we developed a three-dimensional (3D) senescent synovial organoid model using senescent rat SFs. We created the senescent SFs by treating normal rat SFs in monolayer culture with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Senescence induction was confirmed by senescence-associated beta-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining, γH2AX expression, and transcriptomic analysis. Synovial organoids were then generated by embedding normal or senescent SFs in Matrigel. Transcriptomic and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed and the expression of key regulatory factors was evaluated by immunostaining. Transcriptomic profiles of the organoids were further compared with bulk RNA sequencing data from rat OA synovium and single-cell RNA sequencing data from human OA synovium. Rat chondrocytes and RAW264.7 cells were co-cultured with control or senescent organoids. H2O2 treatment significantly increased SA-β-gal positivity and the expression of γH2AX and senescence-associated genes in monolayer-cultured SFs. Senescent organoids had thickened lining layers and distinct transcriptomic profiles compared to normal organoids. Enrichment analyses identified the upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix (ECM) organization, growth factor responses, and PI3K-Akt/MAPK signaling. Senescent organoids had a unique secretory phenotype characterized by elevated expression of ECM components, ECM-degrading enzymes, and proinflammatory factors. The expression of senescence-associated genes was greater in senescent organoids than in control organoids or H2O2-treated monolayer SFs. Protein-protein interaction analysis of senescent organoids identified central hub genes, including Il6, Tgfb1, Mmp13, and Ngf, with upregulation also confirmed at the protein level. Comparison with transcriptomic data from rat and human OA synovium revealed transcriptional similarities between senescent organoids and OA SFs in both species. Co-culture assays showed that senescent organoids decreased Sox9 expression and increased Col10a1 expression in chondrocytes, whereas they increased Cd80 expression and decreased Cd206 expression in RAW264.7 cells. Senescent organoids can faithfully recapitulate key features of the senescent SF microenvironment, offering an ideal platform for cellular senescence-based OA research.

records.title: Dual mTORC1/2 and Scd1 inhibition uncovers a therapeutic vulnerability in pancreatic cancer.
records.abstract: Hyperactivation of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) complexes, mTORC1 and mTORC2, is common in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). However, clinical use of mTOR inhibitors has shown limited efficacy due to rapid adaptive resistance. Using inducible genetically engineered mouse models and matched organoids, we delineated distinct complex-specific adaptations. Loss of mTORC1 delayed tumor progression but induced compensatory PI3K/Akt signalling hyperactivation, while concurrently suppressing inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts and desmoplasia through Il-1ra. In contrast, mTORC2 loss impaired de novo sphingolipid synthesis, shifted lipid composition toward saturation, increased the saturated-to-monounsaturated fatty acid ratio, enriched plasma membrane lipid rafts, and amplified interferon-γ signaling. This lipid reprogramming generated a synthetic-lethal dependency on stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (Scd1). Pharmacological co-inhibition of mTORC1/2 and Scd1 prevented adaptive PI3K/Akt signalling rebound, remodelled the tumor stroma, enhanced interferon-γ responses, and synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy. These findings establish dual targeting of mTOR signaling and Scd1 as a rational therapeutic strategy for PDAC.

records.title: Multi-Omics Profiling of Cigarette Smoke-Associated Changes in Cell Models of Human Liver, Intestine and Lung.
records.abstract: Cigarette smoke is a complex mixture that affects toxicological and pharmacological mechanisms in multiple organs, including liver, intestine, and lung. Therefore, an integrated multi-omics approach was applied to characterize cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced effects across human in vitro models of liver, intestine and lung. Primary human hepatocytes, biopsy-derived intestinal organoids, alveolar A549 cells, primary bronchial and small airway epithelial cells were exposed to CSE and analyzed using RNA sequencing and untargeted proteomics. Across tissues and omics-layers, activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling and strong induction of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 was identified as cross-tissue response. CYP1A1 was the only overlapping molecule among deregulated proteins across all in vitro models. Consistent deregulation of G protein-coupled receptor-signaling was observed. Overall, tissue-specific adaptations were identified. Liver models showed upregulation of xenobiotic and metabolic pathways, intestine models displayed downregulation of cell cycle processes consistent with growth arrest. Lung models should be considered cautiously because of heterogeneity between cell models but demonstrated a shared response of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 deregulation. Cross-omics comparisons of RNA sequencing and proteomics data revealed moderate correlations (ρ = 0.43-0.64) and limited overlap of individual molecules, highlighting the importance of post-transcriptional regulation. Network and upstream regulator analyses predicted a coordinated stress response accompanied by modulation of inflammatory signaling. These findings demonstrate that cigarette smoke induces shared pathway-level responses, alongside tissue-specific adaptations. This underscores the importance of considering multiple organ systems in toxicological and pharmacological assessments. This comprehensive dataset provides a resource that may support further hypothesis-driven analysis of cigarette smoke-related mechanisms.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: AI-guided De Novo design of DHPS inhibitors.
records.abstract: Hypusine modification of eIF5A by Deoxyhypusine Synthase (DHPS) is essential for the replication of a broad range of viruses, making DHPS an attractive host-directed therapy (HDT) target for antiviral drug discovery. AI-based drug design methods spanning binding affinity prediction and de novo molecular generation are rapidly proliferating, yet systematic benchmarking of diverse algorithmic paradigms under identical conditions on a shared target, with experimental validation, remains scarce. Here, we present an integrated AI benchmarking pipeline targeting DHPS and evaluate the full process from computational prediction to experimental validation. We compared 13 MM-GBSA score estimation models and 10 de novo molecular generation methods under 5-seed repeated experiments. For the prediction task, we propose an Out-of-Fold stacking ensemble integrating gradient boosting, graph neural networks, and chemical language models, achieving the highest Spearman rank correlation of 0.861 among all compared models. For the generation task, we propose RL-Design, a reinforcement learning-based framework using the ensemble predictor as a scoring oracle. RL-Design achieved the highest hit rate of 92.02% and maintained drug-like physicochemical properties across generated molecules, outperforming all nine competing methods. Moreover, experimental dose-response assays confirmed inhibitory activity in all three predicted-active compounds, with two highly active compounds showing IC50 values of 31.2 and 49.1 µM. Predicted and experimental activity showed complete concordance across all six tested compounds, providing oracle-independent validation of the pipeline. This pipeline provides a reproducible framework for AI-guided, target-specific inhibitor design and demonstrates the feasibility of HDT-focused antiviral drug discovery through systematic AI benchmarking.Scientific contributionThis work proposes two methods for inhibitor discovery against DHPS, a host-directed antiviral target. A predictive model for MM-GBSA binding-score estimation and a generative model that designs candidate hit compounds both ranked first among previous prediction and generation models under identical benchmarking. The predicted activities were experimentally confirmed by dose-response enzymatic assays.

records.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
records.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fundamental details of these enzymes. To complement these hidden-logic models, we present a structure- and physics-based workflow that mimics directed evolution in silico. This Virtual Protein EngineeR (referred to as ViPER) aims to simulate directed evolution by leveraging computational modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, in silico mutagenesis, and structure-based property evaluation to iteratively engineer an enzyme toward a desired target. In this work, we present a retrospective analysis to demonstrate ViPER's ability to efficiently navigate the complex protein-protein interfaces associated with the oligomerization of a ketoreductase (KRED) enzyme. In addition to successfully predicting >70% of sites that are crucial for toggling the oligomerization of this KRED enzyme (after only five rounds), this dynamics-based methodology identifies a distal mutation that was incorporated during experiment-based directed evolution. This work provides a novel foundation for computationally driven directed evolution efforts, opening the opportunity to simultaneously pursue and evaluate multiple evolutionary routes through a physics-based lens.

records.title: Filling the massive AI drug discovery data gap.
Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization.
records.abstract: Advances in protein structure prediction have created opportunities for structure-based drug design, yet translating structural knowledge into actionable small-molecule ligands remains difficult. Existing benchmarks often use simplified datasets and computational surrogates that poorly capture the heterogeneity and constraints of real-world drug discovery. We introduce MolGenBench, a comprehensive benchmark for de novo molecular generation and hit-to-lead optimization built on a large, structurally diverse dataset. Evaluation of 17 leading methods reveals persistent limitations, including weak virtual-screening performance, limited coverage of target-specific bioactive space, frequent high-risk structural motifs, poor target awareness, and reduced generalization to unseen proteins. Although some models improve three-dimensional conformation generation, they still struggle to produce active molecules reliably. MolGenBench provides standardized data, metrics, and analyses that connect structural prediction with practical molecular design and guide the development of more effective structure-based generative models.

records.title: Roads not taken: The mismatch between safety and regulation of plant breeding innovation.
records.abstract: Meeting global food security goals while reducing agriculture's environmental impact requires continued crop improvement and innovation. Advances in transgenesis, cisgenesis, and genome editing now enable increasingly precise genetic modification with risks comparable to those of conventional breeding, yet regulatory frameworks remain focused on the method used rather than the product. We highlight recent examples, including immune receptor transfer, cisgenesis-based disease resistance stacking, photosynthesis engineering, and AI-guided protein design, that illustrate innovations constrained by current regulatory approaches. A decisive shift toward science-based, proportionate, and product-focused regulation is needed so that improved crops are evaluated on the basis of their properties, not how they were made.

records.title: Structural mechanism of programmable gene integration by the R2 retrotransposon coupled with CRISPR-Cas9.
records.abstract: R2 retroelements are non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons that primarily insert into 28S ribosomal DNA loci across diverse eukaryotes. R2 elements home to their target sites through target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT), in which the R2 protein recognizes and nicks the target DNA to prime reverse transcription using an R2-encoding RNA as the template. The avian R2 system from Taeniopygia guttata (R2Tg) can insert a payload sequence within an RNA template into 28S ribosomal DNA loci in human cells. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy structures of the R2Tg-template RNA-target DNA complex in the TPRT initiation state, both alone and bound to a Cas9-guide RNA complex. These structures provide mechanistic insights into R2Tg-mediated TPRT in its natural context and in the programmable gene integration system STITCHR (site-specific target-primed insertion through targeted CRISPR homing of retroelements). Furthermore, we combine these structural insights with computational protein design methods to engineer an enhanced STITCHR system.

records.title: Comparative reasoning in radiology artificial intelligence: longitudinal and reference-case approaches.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology remains predominantly examination-centric, whereas clinical interpretation frequently depends on comparison across time or with relevant prior cases. This narrative review examines comparative reasoning in radiology AI through two related but clinically distinct forms: longitudinal reasoning, which compares examinations from the same patient over time, and reference-case reasoning, which uses clinically analogous cases from other patients to support interpretation. We propose a capability hierarchy that distinguishes simple access to comparative information from higher-level capabilities, including selection of relevant historical context, anatomical and lesion-level correspondence, characterization of interval change, temporal-state interpretation, multi-interval trajectory reasoning, and entity-specific assessment of clinical similarity. This distinction matters because providing prior examinations or retrieving visually similar cases does not itself demonstrate meaningful comparative reasoning. We review developments in prior-examination selection, registration, lesion tracking, temporal vision-language modeling, treatment-response assessment, analogous-case retrieval, and longitudinal report generation. Particular emphasis is placed on evaluation strategies that determine whether model performance depends appropriately on clinically relevant comparative information rather than on additional input volume, global image similarity, acquisition characteristics, or other shortcuts. Key challenges include incorrect prior selection, lesion mismatching, temporal inconsistency, clinically irrelevant reference-case retrieval, data leakage, misleading comparative language, and propagation of historical errors. Future progress will require models that preserve entity identity, reason coherently across multi-visit imaging histories, identify clinically informative reference cases, and demonstrate benefit under realistic clinical conditions. Comparative reasoning is therefore a necessary step in the transition from examination-level toward patient-level radiology AI.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
records.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: A Review of Osteosarcoma-Derived Exosomes in Tumor Progression, Chemoresistance, and Bone Regeneration, and Their Potential in Drug Delivery.
records.abstract: Exosomes, as critical mediators of intercellular communication, transport nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that drive osteosarcoma (OS) progression and dynamically remodel the tumor microenvironment. Their distinctive biological properties-including low immunogenicity, high stability, and inherent targeting capability-position them as versatile tools across the entire OS management continuum, from early non-invasive diagnosis via liquid biopsy to targeted biotherapy and postoperative bone regeneration through coordinated osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling. This review first outlines the epidemiological features and principal clinical bottlenecks of OS, then systematically summarizes exosome biogenesis, cellular uptake mechanisms, and the key molecular pathways through which exosomal cargoes regulate OS malignancy. We highlight emerging evidence that exosomal biomarkers enable real-time disease monitoring and that engineered exosomes serve as precision nanocarriers for therapeutic delivery. Notably, we emphasize recent insights into exosome-mediated crosstalk with immune cells within the osteoimmune microenvironment, their role in orchestrating vascularized bone formation, and advances in exosome-functionalized biomaterial scaffolds that effectively bridge tissue engineering with oncology. The clinical relevance of these findings lies in their potential integration into a unified diagnostic-therapeutic-regenerative paradigm, which may help overcome current limitations in surgical outcomes and chemoresistance. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains hindered by persistent challenges, including the lack of standardized isolation and characterization protocols, suboptimal in vivo delivery efficiency, batch-to-batch variability, and insufficient long-term safety data. Addressing these obstacles will require further mechanistic studies and multicenter clinical trials to establish robust regulatory frameworks. This article aims to review the roles of osteosarcoma-derived exosomes in tumor progression, chemoresistance, and bone regeneration, as well as their potential for drug delivery.

records.title: An extraction-free one-pot immunomagnetic-RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a platform for ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1.
records.abstract: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expressed on the surface of exosomes (exo) is a promising liquid biopsy biomarker for monitoring response to immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, existing detection methods are limited by insufficient sensitivity and complicated operation. To address this, we developed an extraction-free immunomagnetic recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)-based one-pot high-sensitivity CRISPR/Cas13a platform (iMRO-HCRISPR) employing DNA-conjugated antibodies. Exosomes in blood were enriched with anti-CD63/CD81/CD9 antibody-conjugated magnetic beads and recognized by PD-L1-specific DNA-antibody probes; the probe DNA then underwent RPA amplification, in vitro transcription (IVT), and Cas13a trans-cleavage, achieving multi-level signal amplification with fluorescent readout. Toehold-mediated DNA affinity pull-down effectively reduced the detection background. The platform achieved a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 101 particles/mL (positive detection at the single-particle level), a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 103 particles/mL, and a quantitative range of 103-1011 particles/mL, with the entire process completed in a single closed tube without exosome isolation. Clinical validation demonstrated that the platform effectively distinguished HCC patients from healthy controls (P < 0.0001), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.964. This study provides robust technical support for the ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1 in HCC and for dynamic monitoring of immunotherapy response.

records.title: Early Assessment of Circulating Tumor Cells and Their PD-L1 Expression as Predictive Biomarkers in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients Treated with Immunotherapy: An Exploratory Study.
records.abstract: The prognosis of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) has improved in recent years but therapeutic benefit remains heterogeneous, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers. Liquid biopsy techniques, including the analysis of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression on CTCs (PD-L1-CTCs), have emerged as promising tools. We conducted a retrospective study in a cohort of mNSCLC patients treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs) to evaluate the predictive value of these biomarkers at baseline and at an early time point during treatment. CTCs were captured with the ClearCell® FX platform and then assessed for PD-L1 by immunostaining. Therapeutic drug monitoring of nivolumab and pembrolizumab was performed. Thirty-seven mNSCLC patients were enrolled. The median CTCs count was 35 CTCs per 7.5 mL of whole blood (standard deviation ± 939). PD-L1-CTCs were detected in 51% of patients. No correlation was found between PD-L1-CTCs and PD-L1 on tumor Formalin-Fixed, Paraffin-Embedded (FFPE) tissue. Higher-than-median CTCs count was associated with a trend toward worse outcomes. In contrast, PD-L1 expression on CTCs did not predict treatment response. Most patients presented a trough concentration of ICI at cure 3 above 10 µg/mL, regardless clinical response. Baseline CTCs levels tended to be associated with clinical outcomes, whereas PD-L1 expression on CTCs was not. Early evaluation of changes in these two parameters did not improve outcome prediction under ICI treatment. Larger studies with longer follow-up and more in-depth analyses are warranted to further define the prognostic and predictive value of CTC-based biomarkers.

records.title: The changing role of the gastroenterologist in the management of advanced gastric cancer.
records.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite advances in prevention and systemic therapy. Recent integration of precision oncology has transformed its management, shifting treatment selection toward biomarker-driven strategies. In this context, the gastroenterologist-endoscopist plays a pivotal role as the first gatekeeper in the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Adequate endoscopic sampling is essential to obtain representative tumor tissue and enable reliable molecular profiling. Current clinical decision-making relies on validated predictive biomarkers, including HER2, PD-L1, microsatellite instability/mismatch repair deficiency, and Claudin-18.2, while additional targets such as FGFR2b and EBV status are emerging. These biomarkers guide the use of targeted agents and immune checkpoint inhibitors, which have significantly improved outcomes in advanced disease. However, spatial and temporal tumor heterogeneity, limited tissue availability, and variability in testing methods remain major challenges for optimal patient selection and treatment sequencing. Multidisciplinary collaboration between gastroenterologists, pathologists and oncologists is therefore essential to ensure standardized biopsy procedures, accurate biomarker assessment, and appropriate therapeutic allocation. This review highlights the evolving role of the endoscopist beyond diagnosis, emphasizing the importance of high-quality sampling, repeat biopsy strategies and integration of novel technologies, such as liquid biopsy and digital pathology. A structured biomarker-driven workflow is proposed to optimize personalized treatment strategies across the gastric cancer continuum of care.
